deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. Folio 8v is a handwritten reading list: a bibliography on the anatomy and physiology of the ear and on how sound travels through solids and liquids. It almost certainly belongs to Riemann's late work on the mechanics of the ear and the auditory ossicles. That work was left unfinished at his death and published by Henle in 1866/67 as 'Mechanik des Ohres'. The sheet was later reused, or bundled, with the minimal-surface papers in 'R.Minimal', which explains its neighbours: the previous page has a spherical-triangle sketch and Möbius-type substitutions; the next page is the draft letter about Riemann's minimal-surface paper.

Items, top to bottom:
(1) Lincke, Handbuch der Ohrenheilkunde, Leipzig 1837; v. Tröltsch, Anatomie des Ohres (1861).
(2) v. Tröltsch, Zeitschrift für wissenschaftliche Zoologie IX.
(3) A. Magnus(?), Archiv für pathologische Anatomie und Physiologie (Virchow's Archiv) XX, p. 79. This is probably Magnus on the anatomy of the middle ear, c. 1861.
(4) Kölliker & Siebold's Zeitschrift für wissenschaftliche Zoologie 1857, Bd. 9 (v. Tröltsch).
(5) Gerlach, Mikroskopische Studien aus dem Gebiete der menschlichen Morphologie, Erlangen 1858.
(6) Virchow's Archiv 1859, Bd. 17, S. 25 (v. Tröltsch).
(7) Deutsche Klinik 1860, No. 6, S. 58: Voltolini on the joint at the base of the stapes (Steigbügel). Above it, 'Toynbee's' refers to Joseph Toynbee's otological work.
(8) Acoustics of sound conduction:
- Gilbert's Annalen, with a volume number (read as 88 by the transcription; this is doubtful).
- Annales de Chimie et de Physique T. 35 (or 36): Colladon & Sturm, the 1826/27 measurement of sound speed in Lake Geneva and the compressibility of liquids.
- 'Bd. 3: Nicholson, Perolle': early experiments on sound transmission through solids, presumably reported in Gilbert's Annalen vol. 3.
- Schweigger's Journal für Chemie und Physik, Bd. 34.
(9) Upside down at the foot: further references, probably to Poggendorff's Annalen. They cite Bd. 88, pp. 497–518 and Bd. 91, pp. 56–82 and 179–214, apparently papers on sound propagation or conduction, plus a 'Heft 238(?)'.

No computation is present, so nothing can be reconstructed mathematically.

results.what: Bibliography for Riemann's study of the mechanics of the ear (middle-ear anatomy: Tröltsch, Magnus, Voltolini, Toynbee, Gerlach) and of sound conduction in solids and liquids (Colladon–Sturm, Perolle, Nicholson)
results.modern_name: Literature list / working notes for 'Mechanik des Ohres'
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann's ear-mechanics fragment, edited by Henle (Zeitschrift für rationelle Medicin, 1866/67)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a reference list with no mathematical content. It is consistent with Riemann's known late interest in the mechanics of the ear, which was published posthumously. Its only interest is as a documentary source for what Riemann read.
transcription_corrections: Line 3: 'A. Hagen[?]' is more plausibly 'A. Magnus' (Albert Magnus, middle-ear anatomy, Virchow's Archiv vol. XX, p. 79).
Line 1: 'Ohrenheilkunde' is correct; this is Lincke's Handbuch der Ohrenheilkunde, Leipzig 1837.
Line 7: 'N. 6' is uncertain; it might read 'N. 6' or 'N. 8'. The subject, Voltolini on the stapes-base joint (Steigbügel-basis-Gelenk), is clear.
'Toynbee's' is an interlinear insertion above the end of the Voltolini line, not part of the Gilbert line.
Gilbert's Annalen never reached a volume 88 (it ended in 1824 at vol. 76). The volume number is probably misread, or the 'Bd. 3: Nicholson, Perolle' line is the actual Gilbert reference.
Annales de Chimie et de Physique: the Colladon–Sturm memoir appeared in T. 36 (1827); the 'T. 35' reading should be checked against the image.

The upside-down lines at the foot probably cite Poggendorff's Annalen (Bd. 88, pp. 497–518; Bd. 91, pp. 56–82 and 179–214). The transcribed words 'Unterhaltungen' and 'Versuche des Schalles' are unreliable.
